intro_html: Cumin beef out of Xinjiang is what happens when Central Asian spice meets a Chinese wok. Thin sliced beef gets a cornstarch coating so it stays tender, then hits screaming heat with a heavy pour of cumin and chili flakes. Total cook time is under half an hour once the slicing is done. Each bowl carries 31 grams of protein and 561 calories for about $4.51 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $4.51 a bowl (at everyday cost). A stir fry stretches meat further than almost any other technique, because thin slices coat every grain of rice instead of sitting in a lump on top.
shop_smart: Freeze the steak for about 45 minutes before you slice it. Firm beef slices thin and even, and thin even slices are what make a small amount of meat feel like plenty.
Cumin is the whole point of this dish, so buy it in the larger container rather than the tiny spice jar. Ground cumin in bulk costs a fraction per ounce.
Cornstarch is the cheapest tenderizer in the kitchen. A box lasts years and it is what keeps stir fried beef from turning into shoe leather.
One bunch of green onions and one of cilantro covers the whole batch. Both go in at the very end, so buy them the day you cook.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain, then toss it with a pinch of baking soda, the soy sauce, cornstarch, and the chicken broth until every slice is slick. Let it sit 20 minutes.
Mince the ginger and garlic, slice the jalapenos, and cut the green onions into short lengths. Have all of it within arm's reach, because this cooks fast.
Heat the vegetable oil in your widest pan until it is genuinely hot, then sear the beef in batches, spread out, without stirring for the first 30 seconds.
Pull each batch out as soon as it loses its raw color. Overcrowding the pan steams the beef and steamed beef is tough.
Return the pan to high heat, add the ginger, garlic, and jalapenos, and stir for 30 seconds.
Add all the beef back with the ground cumin, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper, and toss hard for a minute so everything coats.
Kill the heat, hit it with the sesame oil, green onions, and cilantro, and cook the rice separately.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of cumin beef over the same weight of rice in each of 14 containers. Each bowl lands at 561 calories with 31 grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: 3.5 lb beef flank or sirloin steak
steps: Slice the beef thin and toss with baking soda, soy sauce, cornstarch, and broth.
Sear the beef in batches in very hot oil, pulling each batch as it colors.
Stir fry ginger, garlic, and jalapenos for 30 seconds.
Return the beef with cumin and chili flakes and toss hard for a minute.
Finish with sesame oil, green onion, and cilantro and portion over rice into 14 containers.
